summary: Lit in 1884 on the north tip of Quirpon Island at the Strait of Belle Isle; reached only by boat, and its old keepers' dwellings are now an inn.

lens.note: second-order dioptric double-flash light, 1909 (Department report); LHF calls it a second-order Fresnel lens. Present lens not described; the list gives a single flash.

structures.type: square wooden tower attached to the dwelling
structures.note: LHF: 60 ft square tower; lantern and top reused on the later tower, dwelling kept

structures.type: circular cast-iron tower with flying buttresses
structures.note: Built at the Prescott workshops; completed by the report for the year to 31 March 1909; 56 ft base to lantern apex (LHF)
LHF gives 1961; the record's 1962 (Lighthouse Directory) not checked. Coast Guard list: red hexagonal tower 14.6 m; heritage statement: octagonal base and lantern
Keepers' dwellings on Quirpon Island, sold 1998; run as Quirpon Lighthouse Inn by Linkum Tours

staffing.note: LHF's keeper list ends with Cyril John Campbell (1963 to 1996); the end of resident staffing is not stated

access.note: Reached only by boat from Quirpon. Grounds open, tower closed (LHF).

stay.note: Overnight stays in the keepers' dwellings; boat from Quirpon. Confirm with the operator before planning.

facts.agency: Canadian Coast Guard (tower); Linkum Tours (keepers' dwellings)

events.note: Wooden tower; light and fog signal in operation 15 August 1884
Fog complaint by the master of the SS Oregon; inquiry found no fault with the fog signal or the keeper (LHF, citing Department of Marine records)
Diaphone installed 1 November 1906, replacing the fog horn
Old wooden tower replaced by a circular cast-iron tower with flying buttresses, prepared at Prescott
Second-order dioptric double-flashing apparatus, burning petroleum vapour under a mantle; completed in the year to 31 March 1909
Steam fog alarm replaced by an oil plant (Department report, year to 31 March 1921). LHF dates the change to 1916
Automatic radio fog-signal beacon established (LHF); Department report for the year to 31 March 1924 says the beacon was proposed for the next year
New octagonal concrete tower erected with a new head keeper's dwelling
Electronic fog signal replaced the oil plant
Keepers' dwellings put up for sale by the government; later operated by Linkum Tours
Quirpon Lighthouse Inn opened to the public, July 1999
Keepers' duplex declared a provincial Registered Heritage Structure
Lighthouse made a Recognized Federal Heritage Building

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record lists 'Quirpon Lighthouse' (OSM) beside 'Cape Bauld Lighthouse' (CCG). They name one light. The wooden tower (1884), the cast-iron tower (1908 to 1909) and the octagonal concrete tower (1961) are successive towers on the same site; the present one is the 1961 tower.

notes_for_editor: Rich station for the Marine reports, medium for the keepers. Fiscal years: the Department reported to 30 June up to 1906; the report for the nine months to 31 March 1907 covers July 1906 to March 1907; from 1908 it reports the year to 31 March. Each citation names its own period, and the page numbers come from the printed page in the OCR head, each confirmed with corpus.py page. Keepers: LHF's list is the only source for Alexander St. Laurent, Edouard Fontaine's years and all keepers after 1924 (the corpus ends with the fiscal year 1923-24). The Department's keeper tables are matched by position from OCR: the 1908 table pairs Cap Bauld with Edmond Fontaine in one row (cited). A 1905 table places Fontaine, Edmond beside Cape Bauld, Lighthouse and Fog Alarm in adjacent columns; not cited because the match is less clear. Unresolved: (a) LHF says the steam fog signal became an oil plant in 1916; the Department's report for the year to 31 March 1921 records the replacement that year, and the 1916 change may be an earlier step. (b) The 1909 report gives a double flash; the current list gives a single flash, Fl W 15s, and the change date is not in any source read. (c) The Coast Guard list calls the tower red and hexagonal; the heritage statement says octagonal. (d) The concrete tower: LHF 1961, record 1962 (Lighthouse Directory, not read). (e) The heritage statement's 'soon after Confederation' is undated and does not match LHF's 1880 to 1884 chronology. The 1889 fog complaint is known only from LHF, which cites Department records not in the corpus (fiscal 1889-90). The May 1901 ice sentence comes from the Belle Isle paragraph of the ice report; the story attributes it to the report generally. Parks Canada's DFHD page 11735 is script-rendered and gave no text. Chronicling America searches for Cape Bauld returned only incidental OCR pages; no newspaper account is used. Privacy: the 1998 buyer of the dwellings is named in LHF; the story names only the company, Linkum Tours. Edward P. Fontaine and Cyril John Campbell are named as LHF prints their service, with no personal details. Suggested corrections: agency and ownership are the record's own errors (the inn runs the dwellings; the Coast Guard owns the tower). Fact-check 2026-10-27: the 1908 keepers' table page image (scan p.192, printed p.183) was not viewed in this check; the OCR line reads 'Cap Bauld j Edmond Fontaine' and the 1909 table (scan p.172, printed p.165, unconfirmed) pairs the same two on one line, so the story says the table was read from scanned text. Story now states that the 1906 'similar tower' was similar to the Cape Norman tower, that the 1905 diaphone line refers to the next season, and that the Coast Guard (hexagonal) and heritage (octagonal) shape descriptions do not match. Story rewritten where it followed LHF and the heritage statement too closely.
